invariants.description: motor law (exact): f = a f_ref pmf/pmf_ref, j = m f n_H_rev / N_A, i = -F j, v = v_one (f/f_ref) m (1 + n_half)/(m + n_half)
invariants.expr: np.allclose(f_rot, a_eff*f_ref*(E_H - V)/pmf_ref, rtol=1e-12, atol=0) and np.allclose(j_H_flag, m_expr*f_rot*n_H_rev/N_A, rtol=1e-12, atol=0) and np.allclose(i_flag, -j_H_flag*F*1e9, rtol=1e-12, atol=0) and np.allclose(v_swim, v_one*f_rot/f_ref*m_expr*(1 + n_half)/(m_expr + n_half), rtol=1e-12, atol=0)

invariants.description: the motors spin up smoothly: from rest a_eff = a_motor (1 - exp(-t/tau_bundle)) (relative 1e-6), and stays within 0-1
invariants.expr: np.allclose(a_eff, a_motor*(1 - np.exp(-t/tau_bundle)), rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-9) and np.all(a_eff >= -1e-12) and np.all(a_eff <= 1 + 1e-12)

invariants.description: second law: protons only run down the proton motive force, j pmf >= 0; the power used is never negative
one flagellum at the reference PMF swims at v_one; speed rises with the number but saturates below v_one (1 + n_half)
thrust and drag balance for a free cell: F_thrust = xi v_swim with xi = 6 pi eta R (Stokes), F_thrust = m F_one
invariants.expr: np.allclose(xi, 6*np.pi*eta*R_body*1e-6, rtol=1e-12, atol=0) and np.allclose(F_thrust, xi*v_swim, rtol=1e-12, atol=0) and np.allclose(F_thrust, m_expr*F_one, rtol=1e-12, atol=0)

invariants.description: energy: swimming never does more work than the motors take from the proton motive force, P_mech <= P_flag (flagellar propulsion is ~0.1-2% efficient; the rest is heat)

bc_sweep.rationale: zero to eight flagella, motor off to on, membrane potentials from hyperpolarised to a cell running down
